note: Partial bank: only questions on G12 Maths Unit 1 (sequences and series) and Unit 2 (calculus). ESSLCE Mathematics for Natural Science, Hamle 2015 E.C. (July 2023), booklet 340 — key-p1.pdf pp. 354–363, solutions pp. 378–392

items.text: Which value of c satisfies the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem in (0, 1) for f(x) = 3x² − 5x + 1?

Water is running into a conical tank (vertex pointing down) at a constant rate of 6π cm³/sec. The tank is 10 cm high and its base radius is 5 cm. How fast is the water level rising when the water is 2 cm deep?
items.why:
1) Similar triangles: r/h = 5/10 ⇒ r = h/2.
2) V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(h/2)²h = πh³/12.
3) dV/dt = (πh²/4) dh/dt ⇒ dh/dt = 4(dV/dt)/(πh²).
4) At h = 2: dh/dt = 4(6π)/(π·4) = 6 cm/s.

items.text: Let f(x) = 1/√x and g(x) = 2 − (1/6)x³ be two functions. For what value of x do the graphs of f and g have tangent lines with the same slope?
Which of the following describes the mechanical meaning of the derivative?
opts: B. Gradient of graph of functions
items.why:
1) The mechanical (physical) meaning of f′(t) is the instantaneous rate of change, e.g. velocity = rate of change of position.
2) B and C describe the geometric meaning (slope of the tangent line).
3) A (area under a curve) is the meaning of a definite integral.

items.text: Let f(x) = 5x³ + 2x − sin x + e^x. What is the value of f′(x) [at x = 0]?
topics: sum rule, derivatives of sin and e^x
items.review: Misprint in the paper: it asks for 'the value of f′(x)' without a point; the options are numbers, and the book's solution evaluates f′(0) = 2. Key B is correct for f′(0).

items.text: Let f and g be differentiable functions and h(x) = g(f(3x + 1)). If f′(1) = f(1) = 2 and g′(2) = 1, then what is the value of h′(0)?
Which one of the following assertions is true by the Principle of Mathematical Induction?
items.why:
1) B is a geometric series with a = 1, r = 2, n + 1 terms: sum = (2^(n+1) − 1)/(2 − 1) = 2^(n+1) − 1. Induction: n = 0 gives 1 = 2 − 1; if true for k, adding 2^(k+1) gives 2^(k+1) − 1 + 2^(k+1) = 2^(k+2) − 1. ✓
2) A fails at n = 1: 1! = 1 < 2.
3) C fails at n = 1: 3 ≠ 1 (the correct sum is n² + 2n).
4) D fails at n = 2: 2 ≠ 4 (correct: n(n + 1)/2 − 1).

items.text: Let F be an anti-derivative of f. For constant of integration c, which one of the following is NOT true?
items.why:
1) A true: that is the definition of an anti-derivative.
2) C true: integrating a derivative gives the function back plus a constant.
3) D false: the correct statement is ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + c, not ∫F(x) dx = f(x) + c.
4) B as printed has '+ c': d/dx ∫F(x) dx = F(x) exactly, so the '+ c' makes B technically false as well.
items.review: Book key is 'B and D'. D is the intended NOT-true statement; B is only false because of the stray '+ c' on its right-hand side (d/dx ∫F dx = F exactly). Item is ambiguous as printed; use D.

items.why:
1) Let u = 3x, du = 3 dx.
2) ∫3cos 3x dx = ∫cos u du = sin u + c = sin 3x + c.
3) Check: d/dx(sin 3x) = 3cos 3x. ✓

items.text: What is the area of the region bounded by the graph of f(x) = x² − 4 and the x-axis?
Let f be a continuous function on [0, 1] and let F be an anti-derivative of f such that F(1) = −11 and F(0) = 11. Then ∫_{0}^{1} f(x) dx = ?
items.why:
1) Fundamental theorem: ∫_0^1 f(x) dx = F(1) − F(0).
2) = −11 − 11 = −22.

items.text: Suppose the sequence {a_n} converges to 3 while {b_n} converges to −1. Then the sequence {a_n − b_n} converges to
items.why:
1) Limit of a difference: lim(a_n − b_n) = lim a_n − lim b_n.
2) = 3 − (−1) = 4.

items.text: What is the fifth term of the sequence {2ⁿ + 4n − 5}_{n=0}^∞?
items.why:
1) The index starts at n = 0, so the fifth term is n = 4.
2) 2⁴ + 4(4) − 5 = 16 + 16 − 5 = 27.
3) Common error: using n = 5 gives 32 + 20 − 5 = 47 (option D).

items.text: Which one of the following numbers is an upper bound of the sequence {(2n + 1)/(n + 1)}_{n=1}^∞?
items.why:
1) (2n + 1)/(n + 1) = 2 − 1/(n + 1).
2) For n ≥ 1, 0 < 1/(n + 1) ≤ 1/2, so 3/2 ≤ a_n < 2. Terms: 3/2, 5/3, 7/4, … increasing towards 2.
3) Any M ≥ 2 is an upper bound; among the options only 4 works.
4) 3/2 is the least term (a lower bound), and 0, 1 are below all terms.

items.text: If the 6th and the 11th terms of an arithmetic sequence are 35 and 75 respectively, then what is the sum of the first 31 terms?
topics: arithmetic sequence, sum of arithmetic series
items.review: The book gives 'No Answer is given' (its working also gives 3565). Agreed: S_31 = 3565 is not an option, so the item is faulty as printed.
